# app

A [Setu-TS](https://github.com/setu-ts/setu-ts) project targeting `bun`.

## Local transport services

Start these FIRST: the transport plugins you selected connect while the application registers, and
do not retry, so `start` fails against a backend that is not listening yet.

```bash
docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d
```

## Run

```bash
bun run start:dev
```

## What it serves

At `http://localhost:3000` (set `PORT` to change it):

- `/` — the hello-world route in `setu.config.ts`
- `/health` — aggregated health of every registered indicator
- `/live` — liveness probe
- `/ready` — readiness probe
- `/metrics` — Prometheus metrics
- `/docs` — Swagger UI for the API
- `/openapi.json` — the OpenAPI document

## Generate code

```bash
bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate service billing
bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate --help
```

## Production

```bash
bun run start
```

The service runs TypeScript source; a full-stack project builds its frontend before production.

```bash
docker build -t app .
docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 app
```

# app

A [Setu-TS](https://github.com/setu-ts/setu-ts) workspace: one repository, many deployable services.

## Add a service

```bash
bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app orders --template microservice
```

Each service lives in `apps/<name>/`, binds a port the CLI allocates, and is registered in every
other service's static discovery map — so `discovery.resolveUrl('orders')` works from any sibling
with no configuration.

## Run every service

```bash
bun install
bun run dev
```

When a service needs another one during startup, declare it as it is added:

```bash
bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app billing --template microservice --depends-on orders
```

The generated dev runner starts prerequisites first and waits for each prerequisite's `/ready`
endpoint before it starts a dependent. Dependencies are explicit because a discovery map describes
where a service is, not whether this service must wait for it at startup.

## Ports

`setu.workspace.json` records the port each service binds. It is the source the generated
`src/discovery/services.ts` modules are rendered from; change a port there and the next
`bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app` rewrites them all.

If a local process occupies a port, the CLI skips it during allocation. To repair existing
assignments, stop the services and run `bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace ports --reallocate`; it
rewrites the manifest, maps, and deployment artifacts together. It assigns from the base port
upward, so a service still running holds its own port and is moved off it.

## Transport

Services talk over **redis** — Redis Streams broker shared by every member.

Every member reads its connection value from `REDIS_URL`, falling back to `redis://127.0.0.1:6379`
when that is unset. Both halves matter: `bun run dev` on this machine needs the local address, and
the generated Compose stack overrides the variable with the broker's service name, because two
containers do not share a loopback interface.

## Run the stack

```bash
docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up --build
```

That builds every member and starts the redis service they share.

The transport is a property of the whole workspace, recorded in `setu.workspace.json`, because
members can only meet on a bus they share. Every service added later inherits it.

## Test, build and deploy

```bash
bun run test     # every member's and library's tests
bun run build    # one container image per member, tagged with the current commit
bun run deploy   # build, ship to the cluster, apply k8s/, wait for every rollout
```

Deploy loads the images into a `kind-*` context's cluster, or pushes them to `--registry` for any
other context. A member's variables are the names its `.env.example` declares; put their values in
`k8s/secrets/<member>/.env`, which git ignores and no image copies. See `k8s/README.md` for every
flag, and run deploy with `--dry-run` to see the plan first.

## Build and start one member

```bash
cd apps/orders
bun run start
```

Full-stack Bun members also run `bun run build` before starting. Node builds inline shared libraries
and keep npm dependencies external.

# The CLI owns this file and rewrites it whenever a member is added, so edits here
# are lost — the member list and the ports come from setu.workspace.json.
#
#   docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up --build
#
# This is the LOCAL topology. A deployed one uses a real registry, a real service
# discovery backend (`provider: 'consul'`, `'kubernetes'`, `'dns'`), and the
# Kubernetes objects under k8s/.

name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-setu-workspace}

services:
  svc:
    # The name the Kubernetes manifest's comment builds, so `docker compose build`
    # and a hand-built image are the same image.
    image: svc:dev
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile
      args:
        MEMBER: svc
      # The optional npm configuration (registry token, settings) for the
      # image's install steps; see the secrets block at the end of this file.
      secrets:
        - npmrc
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'
    # The member's own variables (SESSION_SECRET, …) from its gitignored .env,
    # when it has one. The environment: entries below win over it, so it cannot
    # redirect a sibling host. Compose follows a link here, and `setu check` refuses
    # a linked member .env; on a branch you did not write, also review its docker/
    # changes before `compose up`, since this file itself can name any host file.
    # `required: false` needs Docker Compose 2.24.0 or later.
    env_file:
      - path: ../apps/svc/.env
        required: false
    environment:
      REDIS_URL: 'redis://redis:6379'

    # does not retry, so a member that loses the race to a backing service whose
    # image cannot be health-probed exits. Compose brings it back until the broker
    # answers.
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Honoured because the generated entry installs a SIGTERM handler; without one
    # the process dies from the signal in milliseconds and this window is
    # decorative.
    stop_grace_period: 30s

  redis:
    image: redis:7
    ports:
      - '${REDIS_PORT:-6379}:6379'
    healthcheck:

# Kubernetes

Generated by `setu generate app` or `setu adopt` — one Deployment and one Service per member,
regenerated whenever a member is added.

## Deploy

```bash
bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace deploy --dry-run   # show the plan
bunx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace deploy             # build, ship, apply, wait
```

It builds every member's image, tags it with the current commit, loads it into a `kind-*` context's
cluster or pushes it to `--registry` for any other context, applies one Secret per member, applies
this file with the namespace and images filled in, and waits for every rollout. Flags: `--context`,
`--namespace` (default: the workspace directory name), `--registry`, `--tag`, `--timeout` (default
`120s`), `--build-arg`, `--network`.

**Secrets.** A member's variables are the names its committed `.env.example` declares; their values
go in `k8s/secrets/<member>/.env`, which git ignores and no image copies. Deploy refuses, naming
every missing variable, before it builds anything, and sends the values to `kubectl` on stdin. Each
Deployment reads its Secret, `<member>-env`, through `envFrom`, and its Secret version is stamped
into the pod template, so a changed Secret rolls it out. For production, keep the values in a secret
manager (Sealed Secrets, External Secrets) and create the same Secret from it.

**By hand.** `${NAMESPACE}` and `${WORKSPACE}` are placeholders, not shell variables: fill them in,
or pipe the file through `envsubst`:

```bash
NAMESPACE=acme WORKSPACE=acme envsubst < k8s/members.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

Probes follow DECLARED health support. A member generated WITH a template, or adopted from a project
that declares `@setu-ts/health-plugin` or a starter, is recorded in `setu.workspace.json` with
`healthProbes: true` and gets `httpGet` probes on `/live` and `/ready`. A member with no such
declaration keeps a `tcpSocket` probe, because pointing one at a 404 would make it permanently
unready. The declaration is a dependency, not proof that the plugin is registered — if the config
never registers it, or it uses custom endpoints, edit the probe paths.

Members recorded with `metricsEndpoint: true` carry Prometheus discovery annotations —
`prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'`, `prometheus.io/port: <the member's port>`, and
`prometheus.io/path: /metrics` — so a Prometheus scraping the standard annotations finds every
member without static target config. Members without that record carry none, because annotating a
member that serves no `/metrics` would make Prometheus report a permanently-down target.

What this does NOT include, deliberately:

- **An Ingress.** Which controller, which host, and which TLS issuer are cluster decisions, and a
  guessed Ingress is one that silently routes nothing.
- **The transport's backing service.** A redis for a cluster is a managed service or a StatefulSet
  with storage, not the single container the Compose stack runs for development.
- **HTTP probes** for a member with no declared health support. A member recorded with
  `healthProbes` serves `/live` and `/ready`, so its probes are `httpGet`; one without keeps a
  `tcpSocket` probe, because pointing a probe at a 404 would make it permanently unready. A
  dependency does not prove registration, and custom endpoints need edited paths.
- **A discovery backend.** These objects make each member reachable by its Service name, which is
  what the generated map's `<MEMBER>_HOST` variables are set to here. For anything beyond a fixed
  list, use the plugin's `kubernetes` provider — it needs the RBAC documented in this repository's
  deployment guide.

# svc
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc
  # Pinned, never implicit: an object whose namespace is left to the caller applies
  # cleanly into whichever one happens to be current.
  namespace: ${NAMESPACE}
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        # Set by `setu workspace deploy` to the svc-env Secret's resourceVersion.
        setu-ts.dev/secret-version: ''
        prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'
        prometheus.io/port: '3000'
        prometheus.io/path: '/metrics'
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
        app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
    spec:
      # Only real because the generated entry installs a SIGTERM handler; without
      # one the container dies from the signal in milliseconds.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        # NUMERIC. runAsNonRoot refuses an image whose user is a name —
        # "cannot verify user is non-root" — and that fails only here, never in
        # Docker.
        runAsUser: 1000
        runAsGroup: 1000
        fsGroup: 1000
      containers:
        - name: svc
          # `setu workspace deploy` builds this member and replaces this line with
          # the image it built. By hand instead:
          #   docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --build-arg MEMBER=svc -t svc:dev .
          # then push it to a registry this cluster can pull from and put that
          # reference here.
          image: svc:dev
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 3000
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ['ALL']
          env:
            - name: REDIS_URL
              value: 'redis://redis:6379'
          # The member's own variables (SESSION_SECRET, …): `setu workspace deploy`
          # applies this Secret from k8s/secrets/svc/.env. The env: entries above
          # still win over it, so it cannot redirect a sibling host.
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: svc-env
                optional: true
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 2
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /live
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
          lifecycle:
            # Covers the gap between this pod leaving the Service endpoints and every
            # node's kube-proxy noticing. SIGTERM is not sent until this returns.
            preStop:
              sleep:
                # Requires Kubernetes 1.30+ (native sleep action).
                seconds: 5
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
          volumeMounts:
            # Only /tmp. An emptyDir over the module-cache directory would MASK the
            # cache baked in at build time, and every pod would then re-resolve its
            # dependencies from the network at startup.
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: svc
  namespace: ${NAMESPACE}
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
spec:
  # The name every sibling dials: the generated discovery map reads
  # `SVC_HOST`, and in a cluster
  # that value is this Service's name.
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 3000
      targetPort: http

#
#   docker build -t <name> .
#
# The tag is pinned, not floating: a Deno older than the one that wrote deno.lock
# fails with `Unsupported lockfile version`, and a floating tag makes that failure
# arrive on a day you changed nothing.

# A member with a frontend (full-stack) declares a `build` task, and its
# main.ts imports the server build that task writes. This stage runs it on a
# glibc image, because Vite's native bundler binding has no musl build; a member
# without the task gets an empty `build/`, so the copy below never fails. The
# task is detected by PARSING the member manifest with the pinned parser, never
# by matching text.
FROM denoland/deno:debian-2.9.5 AS frontend
WORKDIR /srv
COPY . .

WORKDIR /srv
ARG NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc printf '%s' 'import { parse } from "jsr:@std/jsonc@1.0.3"; for (const name of ["deno.json", "deno.jsonc"]) { let source; try { source = Deno.readTextFileSync(name); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof Deno.errors.NotFound) continue; throw error; } const manifest = parse(source); if (manifest.tasks && "build" in manifest.tasks) Deno.writeTextFileSync(".setu-build-task", ""); break; }' | DENO_DIR=/tmp/.setu-build-cache deno run --no-config --no-lock --no-prompt --allow-read=./deno.json,./deno.jsonc --allow-write=./.setu-build-task - && if [ -z "$NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY" ]; then unset NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY; fi && if [ -f .setu-build-task ]; then deno task build; else mkdir -p build; fi

FROM denoland/deno:alpine-2.9.5

WORKDIR /srv

# The root manifest and lockfile first: they change far less often than member
# source, so they earn their own cache layer.
COPY . .

WORKDIR /srv

# The frontend output, built in the stage above (empty for a member without one).
COPY --from=frontend /srv/buil[d] ./build/

# Three steps, and the LAST one is the guarantee. Deno records a jsr package's
# npm edge list NONDETERMINISTICALLY on a cold cache: four `--no-cache` builds of
# one unchanged workspace produced `@setu-ts/messaging-plugin` entries missing
# `npm:amqplib`/`npm:ioredis` twice and complete twice, while both packages were
# recorded in the lockfile's package section every time. Runtime `--frozen` does
# not write the lockfile, so against an incomplete one it REFUSES — the container
# dies at registration reporting a stale lockfile, from an image that built green.
#
# So `deno cache main.ts` compiles the entry's graph into the image, `deno install`
# completes the edge lists the frozen check compares against, and `deno install --frozen` VERIFIES
# it: an edge still missing fails the BUILD, loudly and once, rather than every
# container at startup. With the verify in place four consecutive cold builds were
# complete, and that is structural rather than luck — an incomplete lockfile
# cannot reach a published image.
#
# Together they are the no-external-network, no-lockfile-write guarantee that
# check:deploy --generated proves: it scaffolds a workspace, builds this file, and
# boots its real broker drivers under --read-only with no external network (shared
# loopback).
#
# The chown FOLDS into this same RUN (X10-5): a standalone `chown -R` rewrites
# metadata on every file the cache layer created, so overlayfs copies the
# ENTIRE module cache into a second layer — measured at 563 MB vs 362 MB with
# the fold, paid on every push and every node pull.
# Remove the development-only pin before resolving the production import map.
# Deno 2.9 needs the full-map install pair to complete lazy broker npm edges;
# an entrypoint-only frozen install can pass while the real broker later refuses.
# The parser is pinned to an exact version and may read and write only the

# app

A [Setu-TS](https://github.com/setu-ts/setu-ts) workspace: one repository, many deployable services.

## Add a service

```bash
deno run -A npm:@setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app orders --template microservice
```

Each service lives in `apps/<name>/`, binds a port the CLI allocates, and is registered in every
other service's static discovery map — so `discovery.resolveUrl('orders')` works from any sibling
with no configuration.

## Run every service

```bash
deno install
deno task dev
```

When a service needs another one during startup, declare it as it is added:

```bash
deno run -A npm:@setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app billing --template microservice --depends-on orders
```

The generated dev runner starts prerequisites first and waits for each prerequisite's `/ready`
endpoint before it starts a dependent. Dependencies are explicit because a discovery map describes
where a service is, not whether this service must wait for it at startup.

## Ports

`setu.workspace.json` records the port each service binds. It is the source the generated
`src/discovery/services.ts` modules are rendered from; change a port there and the next
`deno run -A npm:@setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app` rewrites them all.

If a local process occupies a port, the CLI skips it during allocation. To repair existing
assignments, stop the services and run
`deno run -A npm:@setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace ports --reallocate`; it rewrites the manifest, maps,
and deployment artifacts together. It assigns from the base port upward, so a service still running
holds its own port and is moved off it.

## Transport

Services talk over **redis** — Redis Streams broker shared by every member.

Every member reads its connection value from `REDIS_URL`, falling back to `redis://127.0.0.1:6379`
when that is unset. Both halves matter: `deno task dev` on this machine needs the local address, and

# Generated by `setu`. Builds ANY member of this workspace:
#
#   docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --build-arg MEMBER=orders -t orders .
#
# The build context MUST be the workspace root (note the trailing `.`). A member's
# deno.json is resolved as a workspace member, and the root manifest is what makes
# the glob resolve — a context of the member directory alone drops it.
#
# The tag is pinned, not floating: a Deno older than the one that wrote deno.lock
# fails with `Unsupported lockfile version`, and a floating tag makes that failure
# arrive on a day you changed nothing.

# A member with a frontend (full-stack) declares a `build` task, and its
# main.ts imports the server build that task writes. This stage runs it on a
# glibc image, because Vite's native bundler binding has no musl build; a member
# without the task gets an empty `build/`, so the copy below never fails. The
# task is detected by PARSING the member manifest with the pinned parser, never
# by matching text.
FROM denoland/deno:debian-2.9.5 AS frontend
ARG MEMBER
WORKDIR /srv
COPY deno.json* deno.lock* ./
COPY lib[s] ./libs/
COPY apps/${MEMBER} ./apps/${MEMBER}
WORKDIR /srv/apps/${MEMBER}
ARG NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc printf '%s' 'import { parse } from "jsr:@std/jsonc@1.0.3"; for (const name of ["deno.json", "deno.jsonc"]) { let source; try { source = Deno.readTextFileSync(name); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof Deno.errors.NotFound) continue; throw error; } const manifest = parse(source); if (manifest.tasks && "build" in manifest.tasks) Deno.writeTextFileSync(".setu-build-task", ""); break; }' | DENO_DIR=/tmp/.setu-build-cache deno run --no-config --no-lock --no-prompt --allow-read=./deno.json,./deno.jsonc --allow-write=./.setu-build-task - && if [ -z "$NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY" ]; then unset NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY; fi && if [ -f .setu-build-task ]; then deno task build; else mkdir -p build; fi

FROM denoland/deno:alpine-2.9.5

# Which member to build. Redeclared after FROM because an ARG before the first
# FROM is visible only to FROM lines.
ARG MEMBER

WORKDIR /srv

# The root manifest and lockfile first: they change far less often than member
# source, so they earn their own cache layer.
COPY deno.json* deno.lock* ./

# Every shared library, because a member may import any of them by name and the
# workspace resolves that name through libs/. The bracket glob is what makes
# this tolerate a workspace with no libraries: an ordinary `COPY libs` fails
# the build outright when the directory is absent, while `lib[s]` matches nothing
# and copies nothing.
COPY lib[s] ./libs/

# Then only the selected member. Copying all of apps/ would invalidate
# this layer whenever any unrelated member changed.
COPY apps/${MEMBER} ./apps/${MEMBER}

WORKDIR /srv/apps/${MEMBER}

# The frontend output, built in the stage above (empty for a member without one).
COPY --from=frontend /srv/apps/${MEMBER}/buil[d] ./build/

# Three steps, and the LAST one is the guarantee. Deno records a jsr package's
# npm edge list NONDETERMINISTICALLY on a cold cache: four `--no-cache` builds of
# one unchanged workspace produced `@setu-ts/messaging-plugin` entries missing
# `npm:amqplib`/`npm:ioredis` twice and complete twice, while both packages were
# recorded in the lockfile's package section every time. Runtime `--frozen` does
# not write the lockfile, so against an incomplete one it REFUSES — the container
# dies at registration reporting a stale lockfile, from an image that built green.
#
# So `deno cache main.ts` compiles the entry's graph into the image, `deno install`
# completes the edge lists the frozen check compares against, and `deno install --frozen` VERIFIES
# it: an edge still missing fails the BUILD, loudly and once, rather than every
# container at startup. With the verify in place four consecutive cold builds were
# complete, and that is structural rather than luck — an incomplete lockfile
# cannot reach a published image.
#
# Together they are the no-external-network, no-lockfile-write guarantee that
# check:deploy --generated proves: it scaffolds a workspace, builds this file, and
# boots its real broker drivers under --read-only with no external network (shared
# loopback).
#
# The chown FOLDS into this same RUN (X10-5): a standalone `chown -R` rewrites
# metadata on every file the cache layer created, so overlayfs copies the
# ENTIRE module cache into a second layer — measured at 563 MB vs 362 MB with
# the fold, paid on every push and every node pull.
# Remove the development-only pin before resolving the production import map.
# Deno 2.9 needs the full-map install pair to complete lazy broker npm edges;
# an entrypoint-only frozen install can pass while the real broker later refuses.
# The parser is pinned to an exact version and may read and write only the
# member and root manifests, so this unlocked fetch cannot float or touch any
# other file in the image.
RUN printf '%s' 'import { parse } from "jsr:@std/jsonc@1.0.3"; for (const directory of [".", "/srv"]) { for (const name of ["deno.json", "deno.jsonc"]) { const path = directory + "/" + name; let source; try { source = Deno.readTextFileSync(path); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof Deno.errors.NotFound) continue; throw error; } const manifest = parse(source); if (manifest.imports) delete manifest.imports["@setu-ts/diagnostics-plugin"]; Deno.writeTextFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(manifest)); break; } }' | DENO_DIR=/srv/.setu-build-cache deno run --no-config --no-lock --no-prompt --allow-read=./deno.json,./deno.jsonc,/srv/deno.json,/srv/deno.jsonc --allow-write=./deno.json,./deno.jsonc,/srv/deno.json,/srv/deno.jsonc - && rm -rf /srv/.setu-build-cache

# public npm registry; a gate building against a local registry passes it with
# `--build-arg`. An ARG never reaches the running container's environment, but
# its value IS recorded in the image history: pass a registry URL here, never a
# credential — an authenticated registry belongs in a `--secret` mount.
ARG NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=

# After the installs, a root `nodeModulesDir: "auto"` (a workspace with a
# full-stack member sets it) is switched to "manual": under "auto" every
# `deno run` re-syncs node_modules and re-creates each workspace library's
# symlink, which the read-only root refuses (measured: `File exists (os error
# 17), symlink '../../libs/shared'`), so EVERY member failed to start. "manual"
# uses the node_modules this build installed. The root manifest is plain JSON
# by now, rewritten by the step above.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc if [ -z "$NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY" ]; then unset NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY; fi && deno cache main.ts && deno install && deno install --frozen && deno install --entrypoint main.ts && deno install --entrypoint main.ts --frozen && printf '%s' 'for (const name of ["deno.json", "deno.jsonc"]) { const path = "/srv/" + name; let source; try { source = Deno.readTextFileSync(path); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof Deno.errors.NotFound) continue; throw error; } const manifest = JSON.parse(source); if (manifest.nodeModulesDir === "auto") { manifest.nodeModulesDir = "manual"; Deno.writeTextFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(manifest)); } break; }' | deno run --no-config --no-prompt --allow-read=/srv/deno.json,/srv/deno.jsonc --allow-write=/srv/deno.json,/srv/deno.jsonc - && chown -R 1000:1000 /srv /deno-dir

# NUMERIC, not `USER deno`: Kubernetes' runAsNonRoot refuses an image whose user
# is a name — "cannot verify user is non-root" — while Docker resolves it happily,
# so a named user fails only once deployed.
USER 1000:1000

# No EXPOSE: every member binds a DIFFERENT port, allocated by the CLI and read
# from its own generated discovery module, so there is no one number this
# parameterized file could name. The Compose stack publishes each member's port.

# Explicit permissions rather than `-A`: this is a security-focused framework and
# an image should not hand its process every capability. The set mirrors the
# member's own generated `start` task, plus `--allow-sys` for the hostname and
# platform probes the health and metrics plugins make.
#
# Keep build-time resolution, and fail rather than updating the shipped lock.
CMD ["run", "--frozen", "--allow-net", "--allow-env", "--allow-read", "--allow-sys", "main.ts"]

# Kubernetes

Generated by `setu generate app` or `setu adopt` — one Deployment and one Service per member,
regenerated whenever a member is added.

## Deploy

```bash
deno run -A npm:@setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace deploy --dry-run   # show the plan
deno run -A npm:@setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace deploy             # build, ship, apply, wait
```

It builds every member's image, tags it with the current commit, loads it into a `kind-*` context's
cluster or pushes it to `--registry` for any other context, applies one Secret per member, applies
this file with the namespace and images filled in, and waits for every rollout. Flags: `--context`,
`--namespace` (default: the workspace directory name), `--registry`, `--tag`, `--timeout` (default
`120s`), `--build-arg`, `--network`.

**Secrets.** A member's variables are the names its committed `.env.example` declares; their values
go in `k8s/secrets/<member>/.env`, which git ignores and no image copies. Deploy refuses, naming
every missing variable, before it builds anything, and sends the values to `kubectl` on stdin. Each
Deployment reads its Secret, `<member>-env`, through `envFrom`, and its Secret version is stamped
into the pod template, so a changed Secret rolls it out. For production, keep the values in a secret
manager (Sealed Secrets, External Secrets) and create the same Secret from it.

**By hand.** `${NAMESPACE}` and `${WORKSPACE}` are placeholders, not shell variables: fill them in,
or pipe the file through `envsubst`:

```bash
NAMESPACE=acme WORKSPACE=acme envsubst < k8s/members.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

Probes follow DECLARED health support. A member generated WITH a template, or adopted from a project
that declares `@setu-ts/health-plugin` or a starter, is recorded in `setu.workspace.json` with
`healthProbes: true` and gets `httpGet` probes on `/live` and `/ready`. A member with no such
declaration keeps a `tcpSocket` probe, because pointing one at a 404 would make it permanently
unready. The declaration is a dependency, not proof that the plugin is registered — if the config
never registers it, or it uses custom endpoints, edit the probe paths.

Members recorded with `metricsEndpoint: true` carry Prometheus discovery annotations —
`prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'`, `prometheus.io/port: <the member's port>`, and
`prometheus.io/path: /metrics` — so a Prometheus scraping the standard annotations finds every
member without static target config. Members without that record carry none, because annotating a
member that serves no `/metrics` would make Prometheus report a permanently-down target.

What this does NOT include, deliberately:

- **An Ingress.** Which controller, which host, and which TLS issuer are cluster decisions, and a
  guessed Ingress is one that silently routes nothing.
- **The transport's backing service.** A redis for a cluster is a managed service or a StatefulSet
  with storage, not the single container the Compose stack runs for development.
- **HTTP probes** for a member with no declared health support. A member recorded with
  `healthProbes` serves `/live` and `/ready`, so its probes are `httpGet`; one without keeps a
  `tcpSocket` probe, because pointing a probe at a 404 would make it permanently unready. A
  dependency does not prove registration, and custom endpoints need edited paths.
- **A discovery backend.** These objects make each member reachable by its Service name, which is
  what the generated map's `<MEMBER>_HOST` variables are set to here. For anything beyond a fixed
  list, use the plugin's `kubernetes` provider — it needs the RBAC documented in this repository's
  deployment guide.

# svc
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc
  # Pinned, never implicit: an object whose namespace is left to the caller applies
  # cleanly into whichever one happens to be current.
  namespace: ${NAMESPACE}
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        # Set by `setu workspace deploy` to the svc-env Secret's resourceVersion.
        setu-ts.dev/secret-version: ''
        prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'
        prometheus.io/port: '3000'
        prometheus.io/path: '/metrics'
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
        app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
    spec:
      # Only real because the generated entry installs a SIGTERM handler; without
      # one the container dies from the signal in milliseconds.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        # NUMERIC. runAsNonRoot refuses an image whose user is a name —
        # "cannot verify user is non-root" — and that fails only here, never in
        # Docker.
        runAsUser: 1000
        runAsGroup: 1000
        fsGroup: 1000
      containers:
        - name: svc
          # `setu workspace deploy` builds this member and replaces this line with
          # the image it built. By hand instead:
          #   docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --build-arg MEMBER=svc -t svc:dev .
          # then push it to a registry this cluster can pull from and put that
          # reference here.
          image: svc:dev
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 3000
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ['ALL']
          env:
            - name: REDIS_URL
              value: 'redis://redis:6379'
          # The member's own variables (SESSION_SECRET, …): `setu workspace deploy`
          # applies this Secret from k8s/secrets/svc/.env. The env: entries above
          # still win over it, so it cannot redirect a sibling host.
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: svc-env
                optional: true
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 2
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /live
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
          lifecycle:
            # Covers the gap between this pod leaving the Service endpoints and every
            # node's kube-proxy noticing. SIGTERM is not sent until this returns.
            preStop:
              sleep:
                # Requires Kubernetes 1.30+ (native sleep action).
                seconds: 5
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
          volumeMounts:
            # Only /tmp. An emptyDir over the module-cache directory would MASK the
            # cache baked in at build time, and every pod would then re-resolve its
            # dependencies from the network at startup.
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: svc
  namespace: ${NAMESPACE}
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
spec:
  # The name every sibling dials: the generated discovery map reads
  # `SVC_HOST`, and in a cluster
  # that value is this Service's name.
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
  ports:
    - name: http

# app

A [Setu-TS](https://github.com/setu-ts/setu-ts) workspace: one repository, many deployable services.

## Add a service

```bash
npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app orders --template microservice
```

Each service lives in `apps/<name>/`, binds a port the CLI allocates, and is registered in every
other service's static discovery map — so `discovery.resolveUrl('orders')` works from any sibling
with no configuration.

## Run every service

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

When a service needs another one during startup, declare it as it is added:

```bash
npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app billing --template microservice --depends-on orders
```

The generated dev runner starts prerequisites first and waits for each prerequisite's `/ready`
endpoint before it starts a dependent. Dependencies are explicit because a discovery map describes
where a service is, not whether this service must wait for it at startup.

## Ports

`setu.workspace.json` records the port each service binds. It is the source the generated
`src/discovery/services.ts` modules are rendered from; change a port there and the next
`npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate app` rewrites them all.

If a local process occupies a port, the CLI skips it during allocation. To repair existing
assignments, stop the services and run `npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace ports --reallocate`; it
rewrites the manifest, maps, and deployment artifacts together. It assigns from the base port
upward, so a service still running holds its own port and is moved off it.

## Transport

Services talk over **redis** — Redis Streams broker shared by every member.

Every member reads its connection value from `REDIS_URL`, falling back to `redis://127.0.0.1:6379`
when that is unset. Both halves matter: `npm run dev` on this machine needs the local address, and
the generated Compose stack overrides the variable with the broker's service name, because two
containers do not share a loopback interface.

## Run the stack

```bash
docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up --build
```

That builds every member and starts the redis service they share.

The transport is a property of the whole workspace, recorded in `setu.workspace.json`, because
members can only meet on a bus they share. Every service added later inherits it.

## Test, build and deploy

```bash
npm test     # every member's and library's tests
npm run build    # one container image per member, tagged with the current commit
npm run deploy   # build, ship to the cluster, apply k8s/, wait for every rollout
```

Deploy loads the images into a `kind-*` context's cluster, or pushes them to `--registry` for any
other context. A member's variables are the names its `.env.example` declares; put their values in
`k8s/secrets/<member>/.env`, which git ignores and no image copies. See `k8s/README.md` for every
flag, and run deploy with `--dry-run` to see the plan first.

## Build and start one member

```bash
cd apps/orders
npm run build
npm start
```

Full-stack Bun members also run `bun run build` before starting. Node builds inline shared libraries
and keep npm dependencies external.

# The CLI owns this file and rewrites it whenever a member is added, so edits here
# are lost — the member list and the ports come from setu.workspace.json.
#
#   docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up --build
#
# This is the LOCAL topology. A deployed one uses a real registry, a real service

# Kubernetes objects under k8s/.

    # The name the Kubernetes manifest's comment builds, so `docker compose build`
    # and a hand-built image are the same image.
    image: svc:dev
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile
      args:
        MEMBER: svc
      # The optional npm configuration (registry token, settings) for the
      # image's install steps; see the secrets block at the end of this file.
      secrets:
        - npmrc
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'
    # The member's own variables (SESSION_SECRET, …) from its gitignored .env,
    # when it has one. The environment: entries below win over it, so it cannot
    # redirect a sibling host. Compose follows a link here, and `setu check` refuses
    # a linked member .env; on a branch you did not write, also review its docker/
    # changes before `compose up`, since this file itself can name any host file.
    # `required: false` needs Docker Compose 2.24.0 or later.
    env_file:
      - path: ../apps/svc/.env
        required: false
    environment:
      REDIS_URL: 'redis://redis:6379'
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    # The messaging plugin connects to its broker during plugin registration and
    # does not retry, so a member that loses the race to a backing service whose
    # image cannot be health-probed exits. Compose brings it back until the broker
    # answers.
    restart: unless-stopped

    # the process dies from the signal in milliseconds and this window is
    # decorative.
    stop_grace_period: 30s

    ports:
      - '${REDIS_PORT:-6379}:6379'
    healthcheck:
      # Members wait on this: the messaging plugin connects during registration,
      # so a member that starts first fails at app.start() rather than retrying.
      test: ['CMD', 'redis-cli', 'ping']

# source would fail every build where the file is absent (measured).

# Kubernetes

Generated by `setu generate app` or `setu adopt` — one Deployment and one Service per member,
regenerated whenever a member is added.

## Deploy

```bash
npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace deploy --dry-run   # show the plan
npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 workspace deploy             # build, ship, apply, wait
```

It builds every member's image, tags it with the current commit, loads it into a `kind-*` context's
cluster or pushes it to `--registry` for any other context, applies one Secret per member, applies
this file with the namespace and images filled in, and waits for every rollout. Flags: `--context`,
`--namespace` (default: the workspace directory name), `--registry`, `--tag`, `--timeout` (default
`120s`), `--build-arg`, `--network`.

**Secrets.** A member's variables are the names its committed `.env.example` declares; their values
go in `k8s/secrets/<member>/.env`, which git ignores and no image copies. Deploy refuses, naming
every missing variable, before it builds anything, and sends the values to `kubectl` on stdin. Each
Deployment reads its Secret, `<member>-env`, through `envFrom`, and its Secret version is stamped
into the pod template, so a changed Secret rolls it out. For production, keep the values in a secret
manager (Sealed Secrets, External Secrets) and create the same Secret from it.

**By hand.** `${NAMESPACE}` and `${WORKSPACE}` are placeholders, not shell variables: fill them in,
or pipe the file through `envsubst`:

```bash
NAMESPACE=acme WORKSPACE=acme envsubst < k8s/members.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

Probes follow DECLARED health support. A member generated WITH a template, or adopted from a project
that declares `@setu-ts/health-plugin` or a starter, is recorded in `setu.workspace.json` with
`healthProbes: true` and gets `httpGet` probes on `/live` and `/ready`. A member with no such
declaration keeps a `tcpSocket` probe, because pointing one at a 404 would make it permanently
unready. The declaration is a dependency, not proof that the plugin is registered — if the config
never registers it, or it uses custom endpoints, edit the probe paths.

Members recorded with `metricsEndpoint: true` carry Prometheus discovery annotations —
`prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'`, `prometheus.io/port: <the member's port>`, and
`prometheus.io/path: /metrics` — so a Prometheus scraping the standard annotations finds every
member without static target config. Members without that record carry none, because annotating a
member that serves no `/metrics` would make Prometheus report a permanently-down target.

- **An Ingress.** Which controller, which host, and which TLS issuer are cluster decisions, and a
  guessed Ingress is one that silently routes nothing.
- **The transport's backing service.** A redis for a cluster is a managed service or a StatefulSet
  with storage, not the single container the Compose stack runs for development.

  `tcpSocket` probe, because pointing a probe at a 404 would make it permanently unready. A
  dependency does not prove registration, and custom endpoints need edited paths.
- **A discovery backend.** These objects make each member reachable by its Service name, which is
  what the generated map's `<MEMBER>_HOST` variables are set to here. For anything beyond a fixed
  list, use the plugin's `kubernetes` provider — it needs the RBAC documented in this repository's

# svc
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc
  # Pinned, never implicit: an object whose namespace is left to the caller applies
  # cleanly into whichever one happens to be current.
  namespace: ${NAMESPACE}
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        # Set by `setu workspace deploy` to the svc-env Secret's resourceVersion.
        setu-ts.dev/secret-version: ''
        prometheus.io/scrape: 'true'
        prometheus.io/port: '3000'
        prometheus.io/path: '/metrics'
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
        app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
    spec:
      # Only real because the generated entry installs a SIGTERM handler; without
      # one the container dies from the signal in milliseconds.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        # NUMERIC. runAsNonRoot refuses an image whose user is a name —
        # "cannot verify user is non-root" — and that fails only here, never in
        # Docker.
        runAsUser: 1000
        runAsGroup: 1000
        fsGroup: 1000
      containers:
        - name: svc
          # `setu workspace deploy` builds this member and replaces this line with
          # the image it built. By hand instead:
          #   docker build -f docker/Dockerfile --build-arg MEMBER=svc -t svc:dev .
          # then push it to a registry this cluster can pull from and put that
          # reference here.
          image: svc:dev
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 3000
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ['ALL']
          env:
            - name: REDIS_URL
              value: 'redis://redis:6379'
          # The member's own variables (SESSION_SECRET, …): `setu workspace deploy`
          # applies this Secret from k8s/secrets/svc/.env. The env: entries above
          # still win over it, so it cannot redirect a sibling host.
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: svc-env
                optional: true
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /ready
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 2
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /live
              port: http
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
          lifecycle:
            # Covers the gap between this pod leaving the Service endpoints and every
            # node's kube-proxy noticing. SIGTERM is not sent until this returns.
            preStop:
              sleep:
                # Requires Kubernetes 1.30+ (native sleep action).
                seconds: 5
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
          volumeMounts:
            # Only /tmp. An emptyDir over the module-cache directory would MASK the
            # cache baked in at build time, and every pod would then re-resolve its
            # dependencies from the network at startup.
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: svc
  namespace: ${NAMESPACE}
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: ${WORKSPACE}
spec:
  # The name every sibling dials: the generated discovery map reads
  # `SVC_HOST`, and in a cluster
  # that value is this Service's name.
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: svc
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 3000
      targetPort: http

# app

A [Setu-TS](https://github.com/setu-ts/setu-ts) project targeting `node`.

## Run

```bash
npm run start:dev
```

## What it serves

At `http://localhost:3000` (set `PORT` to change it):

- `/` — the hello-world route in `setu.config.ts`
- `/greetings` — the example controller, greeting the world
- `/greetings/:name` — the same controller, greeting `name`
- `/health` — aggregated health of every registered indicator
- `/live` — liveness probe
- `/ready` — readiness probe
- `/metrics` — Prometheus metrics
- `/docs` — Swagger UI for the API
- `/openapi.json` — the OpenAPI document

## Generate code

```bash
npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate service billing
npx @setu-ts/cli@0.10.0 generate --help
```

## Production

```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

The build type-checks, checks CLI wiring and bundles the service into dist/. Run npm test before building an image: DI graph validation happens at boot.

```bash
docker build -t app .
docker run --rm -p 3000:3000 app
```
